title: Eval Cost x Coverage: How Expensive Evals Force Sampling Gaps That Adversaries Exploit

original_idea.body:
# Eval Cost x Coverage: How Expensive Evals Force Sampling Gaps That Adversaries Exploit

**Problem:** Comprehensive evals are expensive so labs/regulators sample; a model can concentrate dangerous capability in unsampled regions.

**Direction:** Simulate a budget-constrained regulator testing k% of items and an adversary who knows which are sampled; quantify how detection drops with budget and how adaptive sampling restores it.

**Why it matters:** Connects eval cost to exploitable coverage gaps. Simulation-only.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2407.14981.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (coverage gaps let dangerous capability hide) but simulation abstraction skips real-eval validation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure stats/simulation study; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped simulation with well-defined detection-probability metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Simulation, no lab access; adaptive-sampling recommendation for oversight bodies.

novelty.reasoning: Sampling/coverage trade-offs are studied; the adversarial-sampling governance framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Coverage-sampling theory exists; the adversary-exploits-budget governance framing may be open.
